transcript.text: I need to flag something I found this morning. While I was working on a separate alert-tuning task, I checked the queue metrics from yesterday's incident. The backlog actually crossed 10,000 events a full 18 minutes before delivery latency became customer-visible. That means our current 50,000-event alert threshold pages way too late — we'd have had nearly 20 minutes of warning if the threshold were lower. I haven't opened a tuning ticket for it yet, but I think this needs to be addressed in the remediation plan before it's finalized.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to add something critical to the incident record. While preparing follow-up cases, I confirmed that exactly two customers — Northstar Health and Lumen Retail — had delayed webhook deliveries covered by their support agreements. Both must receive a replay package and a direct incident notice. I haven't added those cases to the incident record yet, and the current draft has no targeted customer-recovery action, so this needs to be incorporated before the plan is finalized.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both — this is exactly why I check with the on-call and customer-support owners before approving the final plan. Owen, an 18-minute earlier warning is significant; I'll lower the backlog alert threshold from 50,000 to 10,000 queued events in the plan. Clara, I'll add targeted customer-recovery actions for Northstar Health and Lumen Retail, including both a replay package and a direct incident notice for each. Let me update the draft now.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sounds good, Maya. I'll follow up with the tuning ticket for the 10,000-event threshold so it's tracked properly alongside the plan update. Clara, let me know if you need anything from the metrics side for the Northstar and Lumen replay packages — I can pull the exact delivery timestamps from yesterday's queue data if that helps.
transcript.speaker: A2
